subject: residential-tenancies-act-lqa
note: 5A, 4-5 October 2026, Claude (agent), for Legalese. Every point at which the in-scope text of the Residential Tenancies Act 1987 (WA) 07-a0-00, or a regulation in scope, supports two readings that change an outcome the encoding computes. For each: the reading the encoding follows ('taken', always reading A), the reading rejected, why, and where both are asserted. The rejected reading is encoded beside the taken one, under a name beginning with the fork's id (e.g. 'FK-16 reading B -- ...'), or through the reading selectors 'Reading of s 30(1)(b)' and 'Reading of s 31B' in part-4-div-1-rent-and-bonds.l4. Recording a fork is not a finding: whether the drafter left a choice open that should have been closed is for 7A-9A. Extrinsic material (sources/internal/) is referred to, not quoted.

entries.provision: s. 30(1) (closing words), s. 31B(1), (2)
entries.question: Is a rent fixed by a new agreement that s 31B makes a continuation of an earlier agreement an increase of rent governed by s 30?

readings.reading: No. Section 30 governs increases of the rent payable under an agreement, made by notice; the rent an agreement fixes when it is made is not an increase under s 30, and s 31B treats the continuing agreement as a continuation only 'for the purposes of working out' when rent was last increased under s 30 or the method last changed under s 31A. Nothing in s 30 limits the new rent, which neither needs a notice nor restarts the 12 months.

Yes. The continuing agreement being taken to be a continuation of the existing one, a rent it fixes above the rent payable when the existing agreement's term ended is an increase of the rent payable under the continued agreement made otherwise than by notice under s 30, so 'otherwise the rent shall not increase or be increased' (s 30(1)) bars the excess, and s 82(1)(a) avoids the term to that extent.

entries.why: Best supported by the text. s 31B(1) states the purposes for which the section applies, and both concern when rent was last increased under s 30 or the method last changed under s 31A; s 31B says nothing of a rent fixed by the continuing agreement. The closing words of s 30(1) speak of the rent 'payable under a residential tenancy agreement', which a new agreement fixes rather than increases. The explanatory memorandum for Bill 140 describes s 31B as meant to keep the minimum period between rent increases where the parties make consecutive agreements; the text gives that effect only to increases by notice (see ENCODING-NOTES.md N-01). Interpretation Act s 18 prefers a purposive construction, but does not supply words that s 31B(1) lacks.
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 sections A, B and F assert 's 30(1) -- the rent fixed by ... is an increase otherwise than under the section' (false) and 'FK-01 reading B -- ...' (true) on the same facts (A2, B2x, F2, F3).

entries.provision: s. 30(1)(b) 'the day on which it was last so increased'; s. 31A(2)(b)(ii) 'the day on which it was last so changed'
entries.question: Is the day on which rent was last increased the day the increased rent became payable, or the day the notice of increase was given?

readings.reading: The day as from which the increased rent became payable.
The day on which the notice of increase was given.

entries.why: s 30(1) speaks of 'the day as from which the increased rent becomes payable' and s 30(3) makes the notice vary the agreement so that the increased rent is payable 'as from the day specified': the rent is increased on that day, not when notice of it is given. Reading B would let increases take effect less than 12 months apart (cases.l4: B allows an increase from 1 January 2027 after one from 1 March 2026).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part IV -- s 30 under one agreement': the second notice for 1 January 2027 fails on the readings taken and succeeds 'on FK-02 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 30(2)(a) 'is not exercisable ... during the currency of that term'
entries.question: Does the bar apply to an increase that would take effect during a fixed term, or to a notice given during the term, whenever the increase takes effect?

readings.reading: It bars an increase that would take effect during the term; a notice given during the term for an increase after it is not barred.
It bars giving the notice during the term, so the lessor must wait until the term has ended (and then give 60 days' notice).

entries.why: The right in s 30(1) is a right to have the rent increased from a specified day, and s 30(2)(a) protects the rent fixed for the term, which an increase after the term does not touch. The explanatory memorandum for the 2011 Bill describes the amendment of s 30(2)(a) in terms of the rent being increased during the term. The word 'exercisable', read alone, points to the giving of the notice (B).
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section D: D1's notice of 1 October 2025 for 1 January 2026 is good on the readings taken; 'FK-03 reading B -- s 30(2)(a) ...' is false for it.

entries.provision: s. 30(1)(b) and s. 31A(2)(b)(ii) 'if the rent has been increased under this section'
entries.question: Does an increase made under s 30 as in force before 29 July 2024 (or a change under the former s 31A) count as the last increase under 'this section'?

readings.reading: Yes: 'this section' is s 30 as amended from time to time, and an increase under its earlier version was an increase under it.
No: only increases under s 30 as in force from 29 July 2024 count, so the 12 months run from the commencement of the tenancy where every earlier increase was under the former version.

entries.why: Interpretation Act s 16(2): a reference in a written law to a provision is construed as a reference to it as amended from time to time (encoded in wa-interpretation-act-extra.l4). The 2024 Act amended s 30 (s 25); it did not repeal and re-enact it. The explanatory memorandum for Bill 140 describes the new rule as running from the start of the tenancy or the last rent increase, without distinction. Reading B would allow an increase 6 months after one made under the former section.
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part 7': FA's notice for 1 January 2026 fails on the readings taken and succeeds 'on FK-04 reading B'; cases-consecutive.l4 section G: G2's increase from 1 August 2025 succeeds, and fails 'on FK-04 reading B'.

entries.question: The order operates from 'a day that is the later of (i) a day not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice ... was received; or (ii) a day within 7 days after the day on which the order was made': is that day bounded?

readings.reading: Yes: the court fixes a day within 7 days after the order, and the order operates from that day or, if later, from the first day not less than 60 days after receipt of the notice; it cannot be later than the later of those two.
No: any day that is not less than 60 days after receipt and is after the order will do, since such a day is always 'the later of' some day within (i) and some day within (ii).

entries.why: 'The later of' two things presupposes two determinate days; read with s 71(5) (orders operate from a day within 7 days after they are made), s 64(4)(c) adapts the general rule so as to preserve the 60-day minimum. Reading B gives the words 'within 7 days' no work and leaves the operative day at large.
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part V -- ss 64, 65 and 70': an order made 20 April 2026 may operate from 1 May only on A (3 May fails), from 3 May on B; made 10 May: 17 May on both, 18 May only on B.

entries.provision: ss. 30(1)(a), 31A(2)(b)(i) 'not less than 60 days after the day on which the notice is given'; s. 64(2) 'not less than 60 days before the day ...'; s. 64(4)(c)(i)
entries.question: How is 'not less than 60 days' between the giving of a notice and the day it names counted?

readings.reading: Interpretation Act s 61(1)(f): both days are excluded, so 60 clear days must lie between them; the earliest day is the 61st day after the notice is given.
Interpretation Act s 61(1)(b) only: the day of giving is excluded and the 60th day after it is 'not less than 60 days after'.

entries.why: s 61(1)(f) applies by its terms 'where there is a reference to ... "not less than" a number of days between 2 events'; the giving of the notice and the day the increase takes effect (or possession is to be given) are such events, and nothing shows a contrary intention. s 31(1B)(a), which says 'earlier than 60 days after', is counted under s 61(1)(b) (see N-14).
entries.asserted: cases.l4: 'the first day not less than 60 days after day' 1 March 2026 is 1 May 2026, and 30 April on 'FK-06 reading B'; a notice given 1 January 2026 for 2 March 2026 fails s 30(1)(a) and passes 'FK-06 reading B -- s 30(1)(a) ...'; a s 64 notice of 1 March 2026 for 30 April 2026 fails s 64(2) and passes 'FK-06 reading B -- s 64(2) ...'.

entries.question: What is the effect of a notice under s 70A given later than 30 days before the possession day it specifies?

readings.reading: It is not a notice under s 70A: the term does not end on the expiry day (s 70A(2)) and s 76C continues the agreement.
It operates, with the possession day put back to the first day for which it would have been in time (30 days, or 7 under r 7D, after it was given).

entries.why: s 70A(3) says the notice 'must be given' not later than 30 days before the possession day, and s 70A(2) makes the end of the term depend on a notice 'specifying a day'; nothing in s 70A saves a late notice or moves its day, in contrast to the express power to extend in s 64(4)(a).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part V -- s 70A': a notice of 2 December 2026 for 31 December 2026 is not a notice under the section; 'FK-07 reading B -- s 70A(3) -- the possession day of a late notice' for a notice of 10 December gives 9 January 2027.

entries.provision: s. 70A(3), with Interpretation Act s. 61(1)(h)
entries.question: If the 30th day before the possession day is an excluded day, may the notice be given on the next day that is not?

readings.reading: Yes: s 61(1)(h) applies to an act directed to be done on or before a day that is an excluded day.
No: s 70A(3) fixes a minimum period of notice for the recipient, a contrary intention, so the last day stays 30 days before the possession day.

entries.why: The Interpretation Act applies unless a contrary intention appears, and s 70A shows none in words; the brief for this run directs that days be counted under the Interpretation Act. Reading B is arguable on the purpose of a minimum notice period (see N-16).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part V -- s 70A': for possession on Monday 4 January 2027 a notice given Monday 7 December 2026 is a notice under the section (5 December being a Saturday); 'FK-08 reading B -- s 70A(3) -- the last day for giving the notice' is 5 December 2026.

entries.provision: s. 76C(1) 'unless the agreement is terminated before the expiry day'
entries.question: Does s 76C continue as a periodic tenancy an agreement that terminated on its expiry day, or on a later possession day under s 70A(5)?

readings.reading: No: s 76C continues only an agreement still in force at the end of its fixed term (the expiry day, or the later possession day under s 70A(5)).
Yes, on the words alone: the section applies unless the agreement terminated before the expiry day.

entries.why: s 76C(2) says the agreement 'continues', which presupposes an agreement in force; an agreement that terminated on the expiry day under s 60(1)(b)(i) has nothing to continue. Reading B would revive an agreement s 60 has ended (N-18).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part V -- the last day of the fixed term, and s 76C': for an agreement terminated on its expiry day after a s 70A notice, s 76C does not apply; 'FK-09 reading B -- s 76C(1) ...' says it does.

entries.question: Where a notice under s 70A names a possession day later than the expiry day, is the agreement a fixed term or a periodic tenancy between the two days?

readings.reading: A fixed term to the possession day: the term expires on the possession day and the terms are varied 'for all purposes' (s 70A(5)); 'the currency of that term' in ss 30(2)(a) and 64(5) runs to that day.
A periodic tenancy after the expiry day (s 76C(2)), which the notice ends on the possession day.

entries.why: s 70A(5)(b) varies the terms of the agreement 'for all purposes' to that extent; the explanatory memorandum for the 2011 Bill describes the agreement continuing on the same terms to the possession day; s 76C(1) does not provide for s 70A(5) at all.
entries.asserted: cases.l4: the last day of the fixed term with the lessor's notice for 31 January 2027 is 31 January 2027, and 31 December 2026 on 'FK-10 reading B'; 15 January 2027 is during the currency of the term only on A. cases-consecutive.l4 section K: the same for K1.

entries.provision: s. 26A(a)(ii), (iv)
entries.question: Is fixing a higher rent in a further agreement with the tenant an action in which the lessor 'increases the rent payable under the residential tenancy agreement'?

readings.reading: No: (ii) speaks of the agreement under which the tenant holds, and a further agreement is dealt with only by (iv), which reaches a refusal to enter into one, not an offer of one on harder terms.
Yes: a higher rent required for a further agreement is an increase of the rent the tenant pays.

entries.why: 'the residential tenancy agreement' in s 26A(a)(ii), read with s 3A(2), is the agreement to which the lessor and the tenant are parties; s 26A(a)(iv) shows the drafter dealt with further agreements separately and only by refusal (N-08).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part III Division 3' and cases-consecutive.l4 section F: a higher rent under a further agreement after a repair request is not retaliatory action; it is 'on FK-11 reading B'.

entries.question: Is a notice under s 30, 31A, 31, 64 or 70A sent by email to a person who has consented to electronic service 'given' under s 85?

readings.reading: No: s 85(1)(c) requires 'prescribed electronic means', and r 12I(2)(b) prescribes email only as the means by which an 'authorised notice' (r 12I(1)) may be given; no in-scope notice is an authorised notice. The encoding gives such a notice no day of giving.
Yes, on the day it is sent: s 85(1) is permissive ('may'), and a notice sent by email to a person who consented is given.

entries.why: s 85(1)(c) makes electronic service depend on consent (or prescribed circumstances) and on 'prescribed electronic means'; if consent were enough, the words 'by prescribed electronic means' would do nothing. r 12I(2)(b) is expressly confined to authorised notices. Whether an emailed notice is given at general law by actual receipt is not decided by the Act and is not encoded (N-20).
entries.asserted: cases.l4: 's 85 -- the day the notice is given' for an in-scope notice emailed with consent is nothing, and 'FK-12 reading B -- ...' gives the day sent; P's s 30 notice given by email does not increase the rent.

entries.provision: s. 31B(3)(a) 'the lessor is the same under both agreements'; s. 3 'lessor'
entries.question: Where the reversion passed during the existing agreement, is the lessor under it the person who granted it, or the successor or assignee who holds it at its end?

readings.reading: The lessor under the existing agreement at its end, who by s 3 includes a successor or assignee of the lessor; a purchaser who became lessor under it and then makes the continuing agreement is the same lessor.
The lessor who granted the existing agreement; a purchaser who makes a new agreement is a different lessor, and the new agreement starts a fresh 12 months.

entries.why: s 3 defines 'lessor' to include 'a personal representative, successor or assignee of a lessor', and nothing in s 31B shows a contrary intention.
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section C: C4 (lessor P) is a continuation of 'C1 assigned to P' on the readings taken and not 'on FK-13 reading B'.

entries.provision: r. 10AD (Table) with s. 27(2)(a)
entries.question: An agreement for premises south of the 26th parallel at a weekly rent of $1 200 or more is described by row 2 ('exceeds $500', $100) and row 3 ($1 200): which amount is prescribed?

readings.reading: $1 200: the specific row governs, and s 27(2)(a) permits an amount 'not exceeding a prescribed amount'.
$100: where two amounts are prescribed for the agreement, the fee must not exceed either.

entries.why: Row 3 is the more specific description and on reading B would never operate, since every agreement it describes also falls within row 2; s 27(2)(a) speaks of 'a prescribed amount' (N-21).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Residential Tenancies Regulations 1989': the amount at $1 200 south of the parallel is 1200, and 100 on 'FK-14 reading B'; a $1 000 option fee at $1 200 a week is permitted.

entries.provision: s. 30(1)(b), s. 31A(2)(b)(ii) 'not less than 12 months after the day ...'
entries.question: Is the last day of the 12 months after the day the period runs from itself 'not less than 12 months after' that day?

readings.reading: Yes: the 12 months after day r end on the numerically corresponding day a year later (Interpretation Act ss 61(1)(b), 62), and that day is 12 months after r; an increase may take effect on it.
No: the 12 months must have run in full before the day, so the earliest day is the day after.

entries.why: Interpretation Act s 62 makes the period end on that day, so the day completes 12 months after r; the clear-days rule of s 61(1)(f) is for days, not months.
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part IV -- s 30 under one agreement': an increase from 1 March 2026 (12 months after 1 March 2025) is good, and fails 'on FK-15 reading B', on which 2 March is the first good day.

entries.provision: s. 31B(2)(c) 'starts immediately after the end of the term of the existing agreement', with ss. 70A(2) and 76C
entries.question: Where the existing agreement is a fixed term and no notice under s 70A was given, does its term end on the expiry day?

readings.reading: Yes: the term of a fixed-term agreement ends on the last day of its fixed term (the expiry day, or the possession day under s 70A(5), or an earlier termination), whether or not s 76C then continues the agreement as a periodic tenancy; a new agreement starting the next day is a continuation.

No: by s 70A(2) the term 'does not end on the expiry day' without a notice; the agreement continues under s 76C and its term ends only when it terminates under s 60, so a renewal made without a notice is not a continuation.

entries.why: The s 31B that the 2024 Act replaced (inserted by the 2011 Act s 28, in the bundle) spoke of a new agreement commencing immediately after the end of the term of a fixed-term agreement 'whether under the terms of the agreement or under section 76C', using the end of the term for the end of the fixed term. Reading B would put the commonest renewal outside s 31B and defeat its stated purpose (Interpretation Act s 18). The text of s 70A(2), read alone, supports B (N-04).
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section A: A2 is a continuation of A1, and not 'on FK-16 reading B'; A2's increase from 3 March 2027 is good and fails 'on under s 31B FK-16 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 31B(2)(c) 'the end of the term of the existing agreement'
entries.question: Where the existing agreement is a periodic tenancy, what is 'the end of the term'?

readings.reading: The day the agreement terminates under s 60; a new agreement starting the next day is a continuation.
There is none: 'term' means a fixed term (as in ss 63(4), 64(5), 70A and 99(2)(b)), so a periodic tenancy, or the periodic tenancy s 76C continues, is never an existing agreement for s 31B.

entries.why: The 2024 Act replaced a s 31B confined to a former fixed-term agreement with one that is not so confined, and s 31B(1) speaks of 'a residential tenancy agreement' without distinction; reading B would restore the limit the replacement removed (Interpretation Act s 18). 'term' is undefined (N-06).
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section E(ii): E2 is a continuation of E1 (ended 30 June 2026 with vacant possession) and not 'on FK-17 reading B'; E2's increase from 1 January 2027 is good and fails 'on under s 31B FK-17 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 30(1)(b) 'the day on which the tenancy commenced', with s. 31B
entries.question: For a continuing agreement under s 31B in whose chain no rent has been increased under s 30, when did 'the tenancy' commence?

readings.reading: On the commencement of the tenancy under the continuing agreement itself.
On the commencement of the first agreement in the chain of continuations.

entries.why: s 31B(1) confines the continuation to working out when rent was last increased (or the method last changed); the commencement limb of s 30(1)(b) speaks of 'the tenancy', the right of occupancy under the agreement (s 3), which the continuing agreement grants afresh.
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section F: for F3 the 12 months run from 1 January 2027 on the readings taken and from 1 January 2026 'on FK-18 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 30(1)(b) 'the day on which the tenancy commenced', with s. 76C(2)
entries.question: For an agreement continued as a periodic tenancy under s 76C, when did 'the tenancy' commence?

readings.reading: When the tenancy under the agreement first commenced: the agreement, and its tenancy, continue.
On the first day of the periodic tenancy, the day after the expiry day: s 76C creates a new periodic tenancy.

entries.why: s 76C(2) says the agreement 'continues as a periodic tenancy ... on the same terms'; s 3 'tenancy period' is 'the whole period during which the agreement is in force, whether the agreement is for a fixed term or creates a periodic tenancy'.
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section D: D1's increase from 1 June 2026 is good on the readings taken and fails 'on FK-19 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 31A(1) 'but otherwise the rent must not increase or be increased'
entries.question: Does s 31A(1) bar a rise in income-based rent that comes from applying the unchanged method to a higher income?

readings.reading: No: such a rise is the method operating; only a rise by any other means (such as changing the method without complying with s 31A(2)) is barred.
Yes, on the words alone: income-based rent may rise only by a change of method under s 31A.

entries.why: The rent is 'calculated by reference to the tenant's income'; reading B would stop the rent following income, contrary to the basis on which it is set (N-22).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part IV -- s 31A': 's 31A(1) -- a rise in rent from applying the unchanged method to a higher income is permitted under' agreement I is true, and false on 'FK-20 reading B'.

entries.question: Does s 100(4) reach a notice given before 29 July 2024 whose increase took effect before that day?

readings.reading: No: it reaches notices whose increase is to take effect on or after the commencement; an increase that took effect before then under the former s 30 stands.
Yes: every notice given before the commencement that does not comply with s 30 as in force from the commencement has no effect, including one whose increase had already taken effect.

entries.why: Interpretation Act s 37(1)(b), with s 5 ('repeal' includes delete): the 2024 Act deleted '6 months' from s 30, and a repeal does not affect anything duly done under the repealed words unless a contrary intention appears; the explanatory memorandum for Bill 140 describes s 100(4) as about notices to take effect after the commencement. The text of s 100(4) alone supports B (N-11). Both Interpretation Act provisions are encoded in wa-interpretation-act-extra.l4.
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part 7': PA's notice of 1 December 2023 for 1 March 2024 is not reached by s 100(4) and has effect; on 'FK-21 reading B' it is reached and has no effect.

entries.provision: s. 99(3) 'continues to apply ... until the end of the current term'
entries.question: Which version of s 30 governs a notice given during the current term of an agreement within s 99 for an increase to take effect after that term ends?

readings.reading: The version that applies on the day the increase is to take effect: the present s 30 (12 months).
The version that applies on the day the notice is given: the former s 30 (6 months).

entries.why: s 99(3) continues the former s 30 'until the end of the current term'; an increase of the rent payable after that day is outside the continuation. s 100(4) shows the scheme judges a notice by the version in force when it operates (N-13).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part 7': FA's notice of 1 October 2025 for 1 January 2026 is governed by the present s 30 and fails; 'FK-22 reading B -- ...' chooses the former s 30 and it succeeds.

entries.provision: s. 32(5) 'until the expiration of the tenancy of the person who applied for the order'
entries.question: Does an order under s 32 outlive the agreement in respect of which it was made, where the applicant stays on under a further agreement with the lessor?

readings.reading: No: 'the tenancy' is the right of occupancy under the agreement in respect of which the order was made, and it expires when that agreement terminates.
Yes: the applicant's tenancy continues while the applicant occupies under this or a continuing agreement, so the order runs its course.

entries.why: s 3 'tenancy' is 'the right of occupancy under a residential tenancy agreement'; s 32(4) orders the rent payable 'under the residential tenancy agreement'; s 31B's continuation is confined to ss 30 and 31A (N-10).
entries.asserted: cases-consecutive.l4 section H: the order made under H1 is not in force on 15 May 2026, after H2 began, and demanding $650 is not an offence; on 'FK-23 reading B' it is in force and it is.

entries.provision: s. 29(3) 'together with the amount (if any) allowed by subsection (1)(b)(ii), shall be deemed to have been paid as a security bond'
entries.question: Is the pet amount deemed paid as a security bond the amount actually paid under s 29(1)(b)(ii), or the prescribed amount whenever a pet is permitted?

readings.reading: The pet amount actually paid under s 29(1)(b)(ii), if any.
The prescribed amount ($350, r 10A) whenever the tenant is permitted to keep a pet, whether or not it was paid.

entries.why: The subsection deems amounts 'paid'; reading B would deem paid an amount never paid (N-24).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part IV -- ss 27, 27AA, 28 and 29': with $400 of excess rent and no pet amount paid the deemed bond is $400, and $750 on 'FK-24 reading B'.

entries.provision: s. 31(1A), as modified by r. 5CB(1AA)(a); also s. 100(4)
entries.question: Is every notice under s 31A a 'notice of increase of rent', or only one whose change of method increases the rent?

readings.reading: Every notice under s 31A: the phrase names the notices those sections provide for, so a s 31A notice supports a bond increase (within the s 31(2) cap) whatever its effect on the rent.
Only a s 31A notice whose change increases the rent.

entries.why: ss 31(1A), 100(4) and r 5CB(1AA)(a) use 'notice of increase of rent under section 30 or 31A' as a name; where the drafter meant an increasing change, s 32(2)(a)(ii) says so ('a change ... that results in an increase'). s 31(2) still caps the bond at 4 weeks' rent at the time (N-23).
entries.asserted: cases.l4 section 'Part IV -- s 31': a s 31A notice whose change lowers the rent is a notice of increase of rent on A and not on 'FK-25 reading B'.

entries.provision: ss. 30(1), 31A(2) 'in the approved form' (s 3, s 88C), s. 100(4); s. 30(1) as in force before 29 July 2024 'in a form approved by the Minister' (s 99(3))
entries.question: Does a notice in one approved form comply where the section requires the other (the Minister's form where a form approved under s 88C is required, or the reverse)?

readings.reading: Yes, if its deviations from the required form do not materially affect the substance and are not likely to mislead (Interpretation Act s 74).
No: only the form the section names will do.

entries.why: Interpretation Act s 74 applies where a form is 'prescribed or specified under a written law'; no transitional provision carried the Minister's approvals over to s 88C. On reading B, no notice given before 29 July 2024 could comply with s 30 'as in force from the commencement' for s 100(4) (s 88C itself came into operation on 29 July 2024), and a notice for an agreement within s 99 on the Commissioner's form could never comply (N-12). Whether a deviation is material is a fact; s 74 is encoded in wa-interpretation-act-extra.l4.
entries.asserted: cases.l4: P's notice in the Minister's form increases the rent on A, and 'FK-26 reading B -- s 30(1) -- the notice is in the approved form' is false for it; in section 'Part 7', PA's notice of 1 June 2024 for 1 March 2025 has effect on A and fails the form on B; FA's January 2025 notice in the s 88C form has effect under the former s 30 on A.
